Verwood Church of England First School and Nursery
Welcome to Verwood Church of England First School and Nursery
'Be the light and hope'
On behalf of our children, staff and Local School Committee, I am delighted to welcome you to our amazing school!
As a Church of England First School, our vision is based on the Biblical message that Jesus is the light of the world and we are called to share that light (Matthew 5:14-16). We describe hope as having confidence in God's promises, knowing that he will never let us down (Hebrews 10:23). This means that we all aspire to shine our own light in everything we do - at school, in our local community and within the wider world. We are truly proud of all we achieve, making the most of every learning opportunity and helping each other along the way.
Our staff team are passionate about providing our children with the knowledge and skills they need to flourish, both now and in the future; through an excellently designed curriculum, fantastic pastoral support and enriching learning experiences that capture their imagination and nurture their curiosity. We are a school family, committed to working in partnership with your family, to ensure that everyone feels welcome and supported at every stage of your child's educational journey.
We hope you enjoy exploring our website, although this will only give you a small snapshot of all that we offer. All information contained within this website is available in paper copy on request from the school office. Please do contact us if you'd like to find out more about our school. We would love to meet you!
Mrs Annie Nesbitt, Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Verwood Church of England First School and Nursery
Are you worried about a child's mental health
In the UK today, an estimated five children in every classroom have a mental health problem. (youngminds.org.uk)
What is Mental Ill-Health?
Mental ill-health can manifest in many different ways. A child could present with sadness, anger, low appetite, tired, emotional or just behaving differently or unusually. Changing mood is part of growing up and is perfectly normal however if a child is not bouncing back from these changing moods or you have concerns, please speak with someone.
If you are concerned about the mental health of a child please contact the school for advice.
What is the Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service (CAMHS)?
CAMHS is an NHS service that supports children with serious mental health related issues. A CAMHS referral can be made by the school or via your GP.

pageCache.text:
Verwood Church of England First School and Nursery
Sports Premium
Sports Premium
All young people should have the opportunity to live healthy and active lives. A positive experience of sport and physical activity at a young age can build a lifetime habit of participation and has numerous benefits for children and young people’s physical health, as well as their mental well-being. We want children to recognise that healthy competition is fun and rewarding and that supporting and working together as a team can be hugely invigorating.
We aim to offer high quality, enageging PE and sporting activities throughout the school, which is sustainable and accessible to all children. We aim to use the sports funding to increase the sporting and active opportunities we are offering our children in terms of participation, competition and the range of activities we offer.
The School Sports Premium funding is given to schools in order to meet the following outcomes:
1. Engagement of all pupils in regular physical activity – kick starting a healthy active lifestyle
2. Profile of PE being raised across the school and whole school improvement
3. Increased confidence, knowledge and skills of all staff in teaching PE
4. Broader experience of sports and activities for children
5. Increased participation in competitive sports

Verwood Church of England First School and Nursery
Learning
Curriculum
Initio Learning Trust's Curriculum Vision
VALUES: Our three core Trust values are excellence, collaboration and respect.
VISION: Our pupils develop character through a love of learning to achieve and thrive. They are prepared to be lifelong learners and responsible citizens with a global perspective.
OUTCOMES: Every child will leave our schools with the best possible character; resilience, confidence, aspiration, integrity, compassion for others, respect, curiosity, spiritual awareness and collaboration.
The Initio Learning Trust's Curriculum Vision is closely entwined with our Curriculum Vision at Verwood C of E First School & Nursery.
Verwood First School Curriculum Vision
At Verwood C of E First School & Nursery, our curriculum is designed to develop aspirational, lifelong learners who are well prepared for the challenges and opportunities ahead. We believe every child is entitled to a coherent, well-sequenced curriculum that offers engaging and meaningful learning experiences with clear progression over time.
Our curriculum is carefully planned and sequenced so that essential knowledge and skills build progressively over time. High-quality teaching and learning underpin its delivery, immersing children in meaningful learning and developing the knowledge, skills and personal characteristics they need to succeed in future learning and beyond.
We pride ourselves on offering a bespoke curriculum tailored to the needs of our children. While we utilise some published curriculum materials to support our planning, all are based on the Early Years and Foundation Stage (EYFS) Curriculum and the National Curriculum (2014). Our curriculum complies with legislation and national guidance, including the teaching of Relationships and Sex Education (RSE). The published schemes we employ include:
Unlocking Letters and Sounds (Phonics)
White Rose (Mathematics)
Discovery RE/The Emmanuel Project (R.E)
Our approach to teaching and learning is inclusive and ambitious, designed to maximise thinking, engagement and a strong sense of belonging for every child. Lessons build purposefully on prior learning, supporting the progressive development of knowledge and skills across all primary subjects and preparing children for the next stage of their education. Teaching is carefully structured to include guided and independent practice, with subject content presented clearly and concisely to avoid cognitive overload. Teachers routinely check understanding, identify misconceptions and provide timely, direct feedback to ensure all children make strong progress.
Through this comprehensive approach, we nurture a love of learning, a secure sense of belonging and the confidence to thrive in the future.
Our curriculum is enriched through a wide range of purposeful opportunities that extend and deepen children's learning experiences. These include performing arts workshops, visits and talks from religious leaders, special visitors linked to curriculum themes, and high-quality forest school provision. Together, these experiences inspire curiosity, creativity, and critical thinking, enabling our children to apply their learning in meaningful contexts while developing confidence, cultural understanding, and a lifelong love of learning, helping every child to Be the Light and Hope.
Extra Curricular Opportunities
At Verwood C of E First School & Nursery, we offer a wide range of extracurricular opportunities designed to enrich learning beyond the classroom and support the holistic development of every child. Through clubs, sports, leadership activities and community involvement, our children are encouraged to explore their interests, develop new skills, and build confidence. These opportunities promote teamwork, creativity, resilience, and a strong sense of belonging.

pageCache.text:
Verwood Church of England First School and Nursery
Willow Blog
Willow Weekly Blog - 05/05/2023
For a four-day week, we’ve managed to fit in a lot of fun!
The children made us all so proud on Thursday during Potted Sports. As Key Stage 2, we always hope that the children will step up and act as role models for the younger children during Potted Sports and that they did! What excellent ‘Verwood Firsters’, demonstrating all of our core values – respect, responsibility, reciprocity, not to mention joy, patience...the list goes on! We look forward to the Key Stage 2 sports day on Wednesday 28th June!
On Friday, we enjoyed a coronation celebration fit for a king! The children made flags, sparkling crowns and took part in a royally great quiz! To top of the day, the children waved their flags high as they sang our coronation songs beautifully in front of a huge crowd!
Enjoy your bank holiday weekend everyone!

Willow Blog
Willow Weekly Blog - 16/06/2023
Willow have had a wonderful week continuing their topic; ‘Feel the Force.’
In English and Guided Reading we have continued learning about our class text ‘The Pied Piper of Hamelin’ and looking at the differences between myths and fables.
In maths we have been recapping all of our learning from the year. The children have been super resilient in retrieving all of their knowledge from throughout the year from addition and subtraction, to fractions and money!
Thursday involved an afternoon of science in which the children investigated magnet! Through some explorative play, children learnt some new vocabulary; force, magnetic, repel, attract, magnetism.
We ended the week with music, adding actions to songs to help us learn the lyrics!

pageCache.text:
Verwood Church of England First School and Nursery
News & Events
Latest News
Ofsted Report 2023
We are delighted to be able to share with you the Ofsted report for Verwood Church of England First School and Nursery, following the inspection on the 26 and 27 September 2023, which has been judged to be Good.
The report highlights the strength of relationships between the staff, pupils and families. Pupils are safe and learn well. Pupils learn how to be good citizens and understand that people are different. The report states ‘They say that everyone is unique and treated equally. Pupils live out this belief in this inclusive school.’
The wonderful start that our youngest children receive in Nursery was recognised as well as the smooth transition into Reception. The report recognises the hard work over the past few years to ensure we are delivering an ambitious curriculum with a sharp focus on reading.
Please see attached letter from Mrs Anstey and to read the full report please click here.
